name: aSPARK
use_label: Gated AI product team for Claude Code
one_liner: An agile AI product team for Claude Code that gates every feature through spec, plan, build, review and QA.

text.why: Hand a whole feature to an AI and scope creeps, or nothing gets verified. aSPARK splits the work across a Product Owner, Designer, Engineering Manager, Developer, Reviewer, QA Tester and Release Manager, and won't let a feature move to the next phase without your explicit gate approval.
text.take: Plenty of tools claim AI-assisted development; requiring a human gate five separate times, with a reviewable paper trail, is what's different here.
build: No service, no account — it installs into a project as Markdown. Running /spark drives the whole loop and leaves spec.md, plan.md, review.md, qa.md and a release log in .spark/; the QA phase opens a real browser and clicks through the running app.

who.role: Solo developers and small teams building with Claude Code who want AI work checked at every phase, not just at the end.

start.text: Inside a Claude Code session, run /plugin marketplace add a-lottes/aSPARK then /plugin install aspark@aspark; on a new project, start with /charter.

caveat: Requires Claude Code and Git; the browser QA phase (/demo-day) needs a browser integration such as Claude in Chrome or a Playwright MCP server. Newly released, with 24 stars so far.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The aSPARK loop diagram: Specify, Plan, Act, Review and Keep arranged in a circle.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
